name: VSI-Bench
ability_definition: The ability to know your location in relation to the environment or to know where other objects are in relation to you.

task_realism.reasoning: The inputs are genuine first-person walkthrough videos of real indoor spaces (ScanNet, ARKitScenes, ScanNet++), which is close to how a worker perceives a building. The relative-direction, relative-distance, route-planning and appearance-order questions exercise real orientation judgments: where things are relative to a vantage point, and how to get from A to B. However, the model only answers questions about a recorded walkthrough. It never has to orient itself while acting, and many direction questions are imagined perspective-taking ('standing at X facing Y') rather than true self-location.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation is offline and open-loop: pre-recorded clips, no ability to look around or re-observe, no time pressure, and no consequences for errors. The scenes are limited to household and office interiors, with no outdoor, large-scale, dynamic or cluttered industrial settings. Many top models are fine-tuned on data from the same scan sources as the test set, which narrows the gap between training and test in a way real deployment would not.

construct_coverage.reasoning: Roughly half the subtasks target orientation: relative direction, relative distance, route planning, and appearance order, which tests tracking objects across viewpoint changes. The rest (object counting, absolute distance, object size, room size) measure quantity estimation rather than orientation, yet they are mixed into the headline score. Several parts of the definition are missing or weak: explicit self-localization ('where am I now?'), continuous updating of one's own heading, and recovering orientation after getting lost.

format_match.reasoning: The video input is realistic, but outputs are multiple-choice selections or single numeric estimates. Real work expresses orientation through movement, verbal directions, pointing, or marking a location on a map or floor plan. The templated question phrasing is also artificial compared to how orientation needs arise on the job.

transferability_reasoning: VSI-Bench uses authentic egocentric indoor video and includes subtasks that genuinely probe knowing where objects are relative to a moving viewpoint, making it one of the better available proxies for Spatial Orientation. Transfer is limited by passive, open-loop question answering, forced-choice and numeric outputs, a narrow indoor scene distribution with training-data overlap, and a headline score diluted by measurement subtasks unrelated to orientation. Strong scores suggest partial, not reliable, real-world orientation capability.

2024.metric: average accuracy across the 8 VSI-Bench tasks (%; multiple-choice accuracy plus mean relative accuracy for numeric tasks)
2024.human_reference: General adult population. Egocentric spatial orientation in everyday indoor scenes is a general ability, not a specialist skill.

2025.model_or_system: SpaceMind (dual encoder: VGGT spatial encoder + InternViT, fine-tuned)
2025.metric: VSI-Bench overall average score (%): mean of 8 subtasks; multiple-choice tasks scored by accuracy, numeric tasks by mean relative accuracy
2025.human_reference: General adult population. Spatial orientation in everyday indoor environments is a general human capability, not a specialist skill.

2026.metric: VSI-Bench overall average (%): macro-average of multiple-choice accuracy and mean relative accuracy on numerical tasks, across 8 tasks
2026.human_reference: General adult workforce performing everyday spatial orientation: navigating indoor spaces and judging where objects are relative to oneself. No specialist training is assumed.
